body.html: Prasobsuk Ville Hotel is a 3-star property in Kantharalak District, Sisaket Province, set in Nam Om subdistrict. Its main draw is a convenient in-town location near the Kantharalak City Pillar Shrine, Nong Kwang Deet Health Park and Kantharalak Plaza, which makes it a sensible pick for road-trippers exploring lower Isan who want to use Kantharalak as a base before heading up to Khao Phra Wihan or Pha Mo I Daeng. It is not a luxury hotel, but a practical place to stay at an affordable rate, sitting where food and daily necessities are easy to find.

Rooms come in two styles: Standard rooms and larger VIP rooms. Every room has air conditioning, hot water, a TV and free Wi-Fi. The hotel offers daily housekeeping, 24-hour security and is a smoke-free property. For anyone who wants more space or is travelling as a small group, the VIP room is a roomier option for only a modest price bump. Because this is still a fairly new property, review numbers are low, so the overall picture of the rooms and service is best confirmed directly with the hotel before booking.
"Clean room, easy parking, right in Kantharalak town with restaurants and convenience stores close by — handy for a road trip to Khao Phra Wihan with a stopover here."

Location is the main reason people stay here. The hotel sits in Nam Om subdistrict, about 0.4 km from Nong Kwang Deet Health Park, 0.4 km from Wat Ban Nam Om, roughly 0.7 km from Kantharalak Plaza and about 0.8 km from the Kantharalak City Pillar Shrine. Local restaurants, coffee shops and convenience stores ring the area, so finding food is easy. Crucially for travellers, Kantharalak is the district closest to the access road for Khao Phra Wihan National Park and Pha Mo I Daeng — far closer than Sisaket city — so staying here saves driving time the next morning.

To be straight about it: the trade-off here is that it is in Kantharalak District, not Sisaket city. If you need to handle business in the provincial capital or visit the city aquarium, you will have to drive roughly 60 km into town. On top of that, because it is a new property with few reviews, the consistency of service and some facilities — such as breakfast or a swimming pool — may not match the larger city hotels. It is worth checking with the hotel first that it offers whatever you specifically need.

In short, if you are planning to visit Khao Phra Wihan, Pha Mo I Daeng or other sights around Kantharalak and want a district hotel in the THB-500s with parking and shops nearby, Prasobsuk Ville Hotel is a fitting choice for a stopover. It suits self-drivers, travellers using Kantharalak as a base for the Phanom Dong Rak range, and anyone with business in the district. But if you want luxury, very spacious rooms, or the full set of city-hotel facilities, look at options in Sisaket city instead.

A planning tip for a Kantharalak trip: if you intend to go up to Khao Phra Wihan National Park or Pha Mo I Daeng, set off early, as the sights are some distance from the district town and there are sometimes restrictions on opening hours and the border situation. Always check the latest information before you travel. And since the hotel has no breakfast, find a morning rice shop or coffee stop in the Kantharalak market for a local-style breakfast before you head out.
